summary: Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Principal of Aliah University, and Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University and Presidency College, Chennai.
Ariane Macdonald is a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology who studied under Rolf A. Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.

Arindam Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford. His career includes posts as professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under MA supervisor Peter Bisschop and teacher Jonathan A. Silk.

Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the doctoral supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

Arjo Vanderjagt (born 1948) is a philosopher and historian who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arlo Griffiths (born 1976) works in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Harvard and earned his PhD at Leiden under Henk Bodewitz. He held posts at Groningen, held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden, and joined the EFEO in 2008.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (PhD 1784). He spent his career at Göttingen, serving as Privatdozent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).

Arnold J. Toynbee (1889–1975) was a historian who studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), the London School of Economics (~1925–1955), and served as director of Chatham House (~1925–1955).
Arnold Kirillovich Tulokhonov (born 1949) studied at Irkutsk State University from ~1966 to 1971. He served as a member of the Federation Council from ~2013 to 2017.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell (1854–1930) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1888), a fellow of Balliol College, and served at Corpus Christi College (~1888–1926).

Arthur Berriedale Keith (1879–1944) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling and at Balliol College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office and held Edinburgh's Professorship of Sanskrit (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen (1875–1945) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding Copenhagen's first chair of Oriental studies from 1919 to 1945.

Arthur Coke Burnell (1840–1882) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1860 to 1882.
Arthur Evans (1851–1941) was a historian and archaeologist who was educated at Harrow School and Brasenose College, Oxford. During his career, he taught the archaeologist John Marshall.

Arthur F. Wright (1913–1976) was a historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank, he served on the faculty at Stanford (1947–1959) and as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale (1959, 1961).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham (1914–1986) was a scholar of Indology and history who earned his degrees at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held professorships at SOAS (1957–1965) and the Australian National University (~1965–1978).
Arthur Philip McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Parimal G. Patil, Palri Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer (1788–1860) was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Jena, where he earned his doctorate. His teachers included Friedrich Majer, Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf. He held a Dozentur at the University of Berlin (~1820–1831).

Arthur Venis (1857–1918) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as professor of English and later principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1881–1888) and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1914–1918).
